name: s81sl_xrt3q
structural_change: s81sl_xrt3q (STW-S81c-COLLA 10-22, from s81sl_xrt3_b; xrt3 TT -116.66 / FF -27.91, xrt3_b TT -82.99 / FF -25.9): XR8 pin predecode (OT_S81SL_XR_PDC): kind/owner predicates decoded from the input pins into kept flags at the same edge as eb/wb/vb (578 eb -> rwe_c/rwr_c paths, input-to-reg slack +365); hold_margin 0.03 -> 0.06 ns for the zero-logic copy class (vb->vb2, x_eps_m->x_eps, FF -26..-28). Ports, cycles unchanged (bench exact PASS, hops/bwide mutants caught).

job.purpose: S81 slice u_xr successor ot_s81sl_xrt3 (FB): replaces the old xr1/xr3 (functional gap: FFN result transport). Slice parents k8c-f (claude/s81-slicep-k8c-1021) instantiate ot_s81sl_xrt3.

benches.cmd: XR_PDC=1 XR_FOREG=1 bash tools/s81_slice/xrt_bench.sh {RUN}/s81sl_xrt3_b_muthops hops 1 1 6000 raw

benches.name: s81sl_xrt3_b_mutbwide
benches.cmd: XR_PDC=1 XR_FOREG=1 bash tools/s81_slice/xrt_bench.sh {RUN}/s81sl_xrt3_b_mutbwide bwide 1 1 6000 raw

pin_regs.reason: Source-registered (S81-SLICE): every input lands in a flop at the pin and every output is a flop (ot_s81sl_xr header); recipe-3 pin_regs would add a second unpriced stage on every slice seam.

pin_reg_split_why: XR6 fallback (FOREG=1): fault leaves a dedicated output flop (fault <= fcore), no recirculation at the pin flop, so io_flop_at_pins anchors it; no pin_reg_split.
outline_why: STW-S81-COLLA 10-21 FALLBACK: s81sl_xr3 outline 570.24x395.28 enlarged to 596.16x432.0 (pin ranges scaled per face): lower pin density (<=~5.4/um) and wider std channels; no squeeze. | ROOT4-S81POST 10-19: first xr3 (C3, HB 1) kit, from the closed s81sl_xr1f kit: same faces + the band port B (bi 1104 in, bo 513 out) on S (the slice band face: pvrd lands bi from below, bo feeds the svc entry q below). Pin-bound: 9,268 pins; S 3,276 on 570.24 um = 5.9/um sets the width, E 2,214 on 395.28 = 5.7/um the height (as xr1f); ranges spread uniformly per face, scalars 2.16 um, clk at the E-face centre. Util ~7% (std ~16k um2 est.): the 40-60% target is unreachable without cutting boundary bits (slice seam architecture), as xr1f.
